title: Hodge–Tate comparison and the stronger filtered request
as_he_states: Construct the displayed canonical Tate/Hodge comparison, compatible with products, filtration and cycle classes.
plausible_today: For smooth proper X/K over a mixed-characteristic complete discretely valued field with perfect residue field, Hodge–Tate comparison is a functorial graded C_p-isomorphism. A canonical K-splitting of the de Rham filtration is a separate and stronger request.
state_of_art: Faltings1988 Chapter III Theorem4.1 supplies the Hodge–Tate theorem; BMS2018 Theorem1.1(i) gives crystalline comparison in good reduction. Neither should be quoted as a universal canonical splitting over K.
why_open: The manuscript gives a conjecture, not an account of why it remained unsolved; the later comparison theories supply the missing period structures.
worth: Worth an exact historical commentary, because distinguishing a graded comparison from a filtered splitting prevents a false attribution.

title: Does every irreducible p-adic representation occur in a Tate twist of C_p?
as_he_states: Every finite-dimensional simple continuous Q_p(pi)-module is contained in some C(i)?
plausible_today: The unrestricted statement is false; geometric representations satisfying a Hodge–Tate hypothesis have integral Sen weights, and embeddings depend on their nonzero Hodge–Tate components.
state_of_art: BrinonConrad2009 Theorem15.1.7 gives the Sen operator. The character exp((1/2)log〈χ_cyc〉) of G_Q3 has nonintegral weight and cannot embed into a C_p(i); the argument is given in computation_notes.md.
why_open: No explanation of abandonment occurs on the page; the modern counterexample applies to the broad reconstruction of pi and p.
worth: Worth resolving as commentary now, because a one-dimensional counterexample settles the broad reading completely.

title: Can M and a nontrivial twist both embed in C_p?
as_he_states: Can C contain both M and M(i), with i nonzero and M simple?
plausible_today: Yes: an irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representation with two distinct Hodge–Tate weights has nonzero component projections which become injective on its Q_p-subspace.
state_of_art: BrinonConrad2009 Theorem8.3.6 supplies irreducible crystalline examples; §§2.2–2.4 supplies the component maps. The positive answer is this run’s deduction, with twists chosen according to the source convention.
why_open: The pages leave both embedding questions unanswered; absence of G_K-fixed vectors in C_p(i) does not answer this higher-dimensional question.
worth: Worth including a complete two-weight example, because it answers the second question differently from the first.

title: Additional geometric constraints and a smallest algebraic group
as_he_states: Find conditions beyond the unnamed Tate conjecture; consider the smallest algebraic group whose scalar extension contains the displayed operators.
plausible_today: One must first specify the geometric category, the Tate conjecture invoked, and the uncertain diagonal entry of the cocharacter. No unique classification theorem follows from these words.
state_of_art: Faltings1988 and BrinonConrad2009 give precise Hodge–Tate/de Rham constraints; the exact programme is class F rather than declared open or solved.
why_open: The source supplies no reason for the unfinished formulation.
worth: Worth only after scan verification and a precise reconstruction of the requested representation category.

title: Links from Tate–Hodge structures to connections and Monsky–Washnitzer
as_he_states: Ask for a link with canonical connections and with Washnitzer–Monsky theory.
plausible_today: Relative comparison maps should respect the appropriate Gauss–Manin connection and the chosen p-adic cohomology theory under smoothness, properness and convergence hypotheses.
state_of_art: KatzOda1968 §§2–3 constructs Gauss–Manin; Faltings1988 proves geometric comparison; ErtlSprang2018 treats integral affine weak-lift independence. These do not constitute one theorem with the unspecified original coefficients.
why_open: The note is two questions without a proposed comparison morphism.
worth: Worth a cross-reference map now; a new relative comparison project requires a more specific target.

title: What do a two-weight decomposition and an integral lattice determine?
as_he_states: The heading “3 et 1 ???” asks what structure follows from the decomposition and the lattice; K-dependence is explicitly discussed.
plausible_today: The lattice and a decomposition alone do not specify an arbitrary continuous G_K-action. With an existing two-weight Hodge–Tate action, invariants recover the two graded pieces.
state_of_art: BrinonConrad2009 §§2.2–2.4 gives the conditional invariant calculation. The uncertain implication sign prevents assigning a stronger equivalence.
why_open: The manuscript retains question marks and cancels the automorphism sentence.
worth: Worth a scan-led reconstruction, because the unresolved arrow changes the logical content.

title: Barsotti’s formal isogeny question for p-rank zero
as_he_states: Do p-rank-zero abelian varieties with isogenous formal groups have to be isogenous? What about dimension two?
plausible_today: The general assertion is false; the all-slopes-one-half subclass is one isogeny class over an algebraically closed field, and p-rank-zero surfaces belong to that subclass.
state_of_art: LenstraOort1974 §2 constructs simple A_3 and A_4 of types G21+G12 and G21+G12+G11. A_4 and A_3×E are the fully specified dimension-four counterexample. Its introduction cites Oort’s supersingular theorem; Oort1974 metadata was checked.
why_open: On the page Manin is reported to know the dimension-two product statement only in p=2. No later manuscript resolution occurs in this package.
worth: Worth a historical correction: retaining “p-rank zero” rather than silently modernizing “hypersingulier” changes the answer.

title: Simple mixed-slope surfaces and the descent argument
as_he_states: Use the two-dimensional family with formal type G_m-hat plus G11, the one-dimensional product family, and discreteness of isogeny to produce simple examples over fields of specified transcendence degree.
plausible_today: Simple mixed-type surfaces exist even over algebraic closures of finite fields; the stronger statement that every isogenous product is itself a product is false. The exact finite-field-of-definition assertion needs its own proof.
state_of_art: LenstraOort1974 §2 supplies simple finite-field examples. The genus-two Jacobian over Fbar_7 in computation_notes.md disproves the product-isomorphism sharpening. The asserted descent is not settled by a product-locus dimension count.
why_open: The middle paragraph is cancelled and replaced by a descent route; the source does not give the missing descent proof.
worth: Worth a short focused follow-up on the exact isogeny-leaf/descent statement after the false product sharpening is removed.

title: Formal p-divisible groups that do not embed in abelian varieties
as_he_states: Twist a supersingular elliptic formal group by a unit with transcendental determinant; nonembedding should persist after finite or finitely generated extension.
plausible_today: A central transcendental unit gives a valid continuous finite-field twist, with no abelian embedding after any finite extension. Persistence under arbitrary finitely generated extension requires a further spreading/specialization argument.
state_of_art: The Frobenius obstruction is independently checked in computation_notes.md using the standard algebraicity of abelian Frobenius. LenstraOort1974 and Pink2005 provide the checked endomorphism/Dieudonné context; no exact printed source for the full extension clause was recovered.
why_open: The source says the unit is easy to find and suppresses the descent and specialization steps; it does not state why the problem was dropped.
worth: Worth a separate proof audit of the finitely generated extension clause, with finite-field descent fixed first.

title: Extension deformation torsors beyond the ordinary case
as_he_states: Describe the extension moduli as a formal torus or torsor and reduce the deformation of E_0 to that of its connected part N_0.
plausible_today: For ordinary étale-by-multiplicative p-divisible groups the Serre–Tate formal torus is exact. For a varying connected nonmultiplicative part, specify the base, framing and acting formal group before asserting a torsor.
state_of_art: Katz1981 Theorems1.2.1 and2.1 establish the ordinary case and its compatibility. The exact larger torsor statement was not matched by the targeted searches.
why_open: The handwritten Tate lifting aside is compressed; no proof of the general representability/action is given.
worth: Worth formulating the nonmultiplicative case precisely; the ordinary case is already a completed theorem.

title: Flatness and the local rings of ordinary polarized moduli
as_he_states: The kernel calculation should imply complete intersection, Gorenstein, local irreducibility, smooth reduced ring and dimension g(g+1)/2; a flatness doubt is cancelled.
plausible_today: For the framed ordinary polarized deformation functor the character equations of a formal torus give the asserted characteristic-p local ring properties. Mixed-characteristic flatness and coarse quotient singularities need separate hypotheses.
state_of_art: Katz1981 Theorem2.1(3)–(4) gives symmetry and morphism lifting. Smith form gives k[[z]]/(z_j^(p^e_j)); the independent algebra proof is recorded. This does not interpret the cancelled flatness wording.
why_open: The source revises the flatness aside and explicitly confines the conclusion to ordinary abelian varieties.
worth: Worth a scan and coordinate audit of the polarization type; no new general moduli theorem is claimed here.

title: Exact Witt extension statements over an arbitrary characteristic-p base
as_he_states: Verify the Frobenius-skew freeness, the restriction and V maps, and the induction for H=G_a or the specified finite locally free additive subgroup.
plausible_today: Separate sheaf Ext from global Ext and track which variable supplies each left or right skew action; the undefined a_2 arrow must be read before a full theorem is fixed.

worth: Worth a source-led audit of the two exact Demazure–Gabriel locators before any claim of novelty or generality.

title: The immediately rejected global Ext vanishing
as_he_states: Ask whether sheaf vanishing implies global Ext^1(H,W)=0 on affine imperfect fields; answer “Non déjà pour H=alpha_p”.
plausible_today: The local-to-global distinction must be retained. The familiar k/k^p calculation for alpha_p is not automatically the displayed Ext group without specifying the Witt direct system.
state_of_art: Pink2005 Proposition22.2 supports a perfect-field transition calculation. The exact global counterexample and imperfect-field dévissage remain unverified source conventions, not a new claimed open theorem.
why_open: Grothendieck himself rejects the global question immediately and cancels the separate smooth-Hom paragraph and following relations.

title: Étale p-primary groups and unit F-crystals
as_he_states: Verify the anti-equivalence, recovery by Frobenius fixed sections, and passage from fixed levels to sums of levels.
plausible_today: Finite locally free unit Frobenius modules over an F_p-base correspond to finite locally constant F_p-sheaves; Witt-level versions require a fixed torsion/free category and the chosen covariant or contravariant dual convention.
state_of_art: BhattScholze2023 Proposition3.4 proves the F_p correspondence for arbitrary commutative F_p-algebras and traces the vector-bundle case to Katz1973 Proposition4.1.1. SGA1 I§8 gives nilpotent étale invariance. The RHom formula in the manuscript needs a cohomological shift.
why_open: The author expressly writes “vérifier” at the anti-equivalence; the underlying categories are partly schematic.
worth: Worth finishing the convention table, because the fixed-point theorem is established but the written duality formula is not literally correct.

title: What is the Witt-module category on scan066?
as_he_states: Propose a Witt-module/crystal category at the end of the fixed-vector argument.
plausible_today: A determinate statement requires the meaning of the completion, the F and V operators, the torsion bounds, and the levelwise or projective convention.

title: Is the intended Artin–Rees pro-category abelian?
as_he_states: Make the pro-module category and its bounded-order differential operators precise; the marginal name is transcribed “Artin–Riesz”.
plausible_today: The category of all pro-objects in an abelian category is abelian, but that does not by itself establish abelianness or closure of the intended restricted Artin–Rees subcategory.
state_of_art: Fiorot2011 §2 and Theorems5.6,6.2 give an explicit bounded coherent pro-module framework for smooth finite-type C-schemes. The exact broader manuscript subcategory has not been identified.
why_open: The author is revising the target from ordinary sheaves to pro-modules and explicitly marks the categorical question.
worth: Worth a precise category definition and closure check once the page order 005→059→006 is restored in the commentary.

title: Resolution, inverse limits and the infinitesimal flatness condition
as_he_states: Use the augmented principal-parts resolution, commute cohomology with the inverse system and identify flatness from exactness of the formalized de Rham complex.
plausible_today: Over Q and smooth finite-type hypotheses, the formal Poincaré lemma and coherent pro formulation hold. Arbitrary inverse systems require Mittag–Leffler or derived-limit control; the unnamed flatness notion must be fixed.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1968 §§6.1–6.5 supplies the formalization proof; Fiorot2011 Theorems2.10 and5.6 supplies a precise coherent pro setting. Neither licenses arbitrary underived lim or every module flatness test.
why_open: The source labels the flatness/limit steps as questions and corrects several target categories.
worth: Worth isolating the exact limit hypothesis; a small counterexample audit can resolve the remaining inference risk.

title: Why the initial non-PD p-adic hope fails
as_he_states: Hope the infinitesimal/stratification cohomology is the desired p-adic theory, even for smooth projective varieties; then record “C’est faux”.
plausible_today: The ordinary infinitesimal site is a different object from the PD crystalline site. Its proper characteristic-p cohomology detects an étale/unit-root part, so it cannot recover all abelian cohomology.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1968 §6.5 retains the counterargument. Ogus1975 Example3.7, Theorem4.6, Theorem4.9 and Corollary4.11 identify the non-PD theory with the Frobenius-stable part under the stated smooth-proper embedding hypotheses. His proof of4.9 flags an unchecked compatibility. PD crystalline cohomology retains all slopes and is a different theory.
why_open: The source gives the reason explicitly: an ordinary abelian variety has vanishing in degrees where the desired cohomology does not vanish.
worth: Worth making this withdrawal central to the historical narrative; it explains the change of site.

title: A weak-lifting site with affine and proper comparison tests
as_he_states: Replace nilpotent thickenings by larger W–M spaces; recover affine W–M and proper formal de Rham cohomology, at least modulo torsion, then remove flatness and field-base restrictions.
plausible_today: Rational weak/rigid theories satisfy precise globalization and comparison theorems. An integral site with all the draft’s intended tests needs an exact topology and coefficient category; lim cannot simply be exchanged with inverting p.
state_of_art: MonskyWashnitzer1964 announces formal cohomology sheaves; vanDerPut1986 §§2–4 establishes the rational affine framework; Grothendieck1968 §7.5 makes a further PD-based site proposal.
why_open: The manuscript calls this a first sketch and states that successful tests would still require substantial generalization.
worth: Worth comparing the two actual draft sites and their test morphisms before proposing another universal theory.

title: Degree-one de Rham dimension, Picard and torsion
as_he_states: Explain excess de Rham H^1 over twice the Picard dimension and ask whether integral torsion matches that of a generic fibre.
plausible_today: For a smooth proper variety the Picard/crystalline comparison must specify perfectness and reduced Picard identity component. Generic étale and crystalline torsion satisfy inequalities in the good-reduction setting, not universal equality.
state_of_art: BMS2018 Theorem1.1(ii) and Theorem2.1 settle the proposed universal torsion equality negatively. They do not prove an exact Picard formula for all nonliftable varieties; that narrower residual is retained.
why_open: The source tentatively attributes the excess to torsion and asks the comparison question; no explanation of abandonment occurs here.
worth: Worth a precise low-degree Picard/crystalline theorem lookup; the broad torsion equality is already disproved.

title: Singular varieties and the ordinary-cusp example
as_he_states: Use an ordinary cusp to show that naive Kähler–de Rham cohomology has the wrong first Betti number; seek a theory handling singular fibres.
plausible_today: The affine ordinary cusp over C has acyclic positive-degree full Kähler–de Rham complex. Genuine failure examples exist for other singularities; completed ambient de Rham cohomology is a different construction.
state_of_art: The Euler contraction independently refutes the cusp example. ArapuraKang2011 Proposition4.2 and Example4.4 give a non-quasihomogeneous curve with excess analytic Kähler–de Rham H^1; Hartshorne1975 IV.1.1–IV.2.1 proves the completed-ambient comparison.
why_open: The source does not correct its specific cusp example in this packet; the abbreviated singularity word remains an ink question.
worth: Worth a prominent correction with the full Ω² term displayed, because discarding it creates a false counterexample.

title: A good coefficient category with Leray and duality
as_he_states: Construct a coefficient formalism for de Rham cohomology, differential operators, homology and exceptional operations, including singularities.
plausible_today: Several established coefficient theories solve precise portions. A universal theorem needs explicit boundedness, coherence, singularity and support assumptions.
state_of_art: KatzOda1968 §4 gives a relative de Rham Leray sequence, Fiorot2011 Theorem5.6 a bounded coherent pro equivalence, and Hartshorne1975 II–IV completed de Rham cohomology and duality. These are not interchangeable scopes.
why_open: The source itself describes the overall synthesis as a programme and its link with W–M as heuristic.
worth: Worth a requirements table tying each operation to a precise existing category; no unrestricted novelty claim is supported.

title: Finiteness and independence of ell in positive characteristic
as_he_states: Ask for general finiteness, independence of ranks and integral characteristic polynomials, while fearing dependence on resolution.
plausible_today: For finite-type schemes and invertible torsion coefficients the étale finiteness theorems apply; degreewise ell-independent integral endomorphism polynomials are established for smooth projective varieties via finite-field spreading and Weil cohomology.
state_of_art: For ordinary cohomology, Deligne SGA4½ ExposéVII Theorem1.1 proves constructibility over regular bases of dimension≤1, hence finiteness over a field. SGA4 XIX5.1 alone is resolution-dependent; XVII5.3.6–5.3.8 handles compact supports. KatzMessing1974 Theorem2(2) gives integral, theory-independent correspondence polynomials for smooth projective finite-field varieties; spreading out supplies the stated algebraically closed-field consequence.
why_open: The manuscript records the state of the author’s knowledge; later finiteness proofs remove the stated dependence on general resolution.
worth: Worth a scope-sensitive historical note; arbitrary singular/nonproper independence questions must not be inferred solved.

title: Flat-cohomological duality and a p-adic coefficient theory
as_he_states: Circumvent Serre’s Q_p obstruction using Witt vectors and connect the desired theory with Raynaud’s flat-cohomological curve/class-field ideas.
plausible_today: Q_p coefficients cannot support the reconstructed Weil axioms over all characteristic-p varieties; Witt-valued crystalline theories and finite-flat duality are distinct precise solutions to parts of the programme.
state_of_art: The quaternion argument is independently checked. ArtinMilne1976 develops duality of flat cohomology of smooth complete curves with finite flat coefficients; BMS2018 supplies the modern proper integral comparison. The manuscript’s Raynaud attribution does not specify an exact theorem.
why_open: The text gives the coefficient obstruction but only an outline for the flat-duality connection.
worth: Worth identifying the original Raynaud source and exact coefficient groups before treating this as one settled or open problem.

title: Proper formal lift independence and integral torsion
as_he_states: Expect finite W-modules depending only on the smooth proper special fibre; ask what their torsion means.
plausible_today: Crystalline cohomology is finite over W for smooth proper special fibres and compares with completed de Rham cohomology of a smooth proper formal lift. Torsion need not equal generic-fibre étale torsion.
state_of_art: Berthelot1974, and the precise good-reduction statements of BMS2018 Theorem1.1, establish the comparison framework. BMS Theorem2.1 gives strict torsion inequality.
why_open: The manuscript attributes partial results to Monsky and Washnitzer and reserves the torsion question for the seminar.
worth: Worth a concise separation of proper finiteness, lift independence and torsion comparison, which require different arguments.

title: Are ideals of weak completions closed?
as_he_states: Ask whether all ideals are automatically closed in the intended W–M algebra.
plausible_today: For a noetherian weakly complete finitely generated W-algebra with the p-adic topology, p lies in the Jacobson radical and Krull intersection makes every quotient p-adically separated, hence every ideal closed.
state_of_art: vanDerPut1986 Proposition2.2 establishes noetherianity. The independent Jacobson-radical/Krull-intersection proof in computation_notes.md proves p-adic closedness for every ideal. The page names no topology, so this settles the usual adic formulation rather than every possible topology.
why_open: The source leaves the topology implicit, so the wording itself remains incomplete.
worth: Worth resolving by fixing the topology; in the standard adic sense the algebraic proof is short.

title: Weak lifts and continuous differentials
as_he_states: Construct flat W–M lifts, prove uniqueness up to nonunique isomorphism, and define continuous Ω¹ and its universal property.
plausible_today: Smooth finite-type residue algebras admit smooth weak lifts; their universal finite continuous differential modules are finite projective, with the appropriate exterior de Rham complex.
state_of_art: SGA1 III§6 Corollaries8 and10 establish the affine infinitesimal and formal lift statement. vanDerPut1986 §§2.3 and2.4, especially2.4.4, supplies the weak-completion/differential formulation and rational homotopy; ErtlSprang2018 Proposition1, Proposition2 and Lemma3 supply integral invariance.
why_open: The draft leaves several assertions for proof and contains a missing Ω¹ factor and repeated A′ in its arrow.
worth: Worth a source-and-notation correction; the standard theorem is established.

title: Integral independence of Monsky–Washnitzer lifts and maps
as_he_states: Show cohomology depends only on reduction modulo p and that nearby lifting maps give identical maps.
plausible_today: For smooth affine varieties over perfect fields, integral Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology is canonically functorial and independent of weak lifts in every degree.
state_of_art: ErtlSprang2018 Propositions1–2 and Lemma3 give the exact integral homotopy and independence results; the preprint was first posted2017-09-21.
why_open: The source doubts whether lift independence requires inverting p; no proof is supplied at this point.
worth: Worth closing with the exact integral theorem and separating it from finite generation.

title: Integral Monsky–Washnitzer finite generation and the rational programme
as_he_states: Expect finite W-modules and the usual Leray, Künneth, duality and trace formalism.
plausible_today: Integral finite generation fails even for A¹ through unbounded p-torsion; modulo torsion it can still fail. Rational theories have finiteness and operations with appropriate supports and coefficient categories.
state_of_art: vanDerPut1986 gives the rational affine formalism and trace discussion; ErtlShiho2020 gives an exact negative result for integral finiteness. The manuscript bundles finiteness, duality, Künneth, trace formulas and unspecified relative coefficients. The checked sources do not constitute one exact theorem resolving that entire bundled programme. In particular, a modern rational coefficient theory must specify support and convergence, and cannot be substituted for the false integral claim. The independently verified A¹ calculation gives unbounded integral torsion; ErtlShiho2020 Theorem0.1 gives non-finite-generation even modulo torsion.
why_open: The manuscript records strong dissatisfaction with nonproper and relative theories, rather than a proof of impossibility.
worth: Worth replacing the false integral expectation by a precise finite-lattice question for a specified geometric class.

title: Canonical and transitive comparisons between nearby liftings
as_he_states: Encode liftings as sections of a smooth parameter family and obtain transitive canonical comparisons, at first modulo torsion.
plausible_today: Derived base change is insufficient by itself for ordinary cohomology pullbacks; local freeness/Tor vanishing and a suitable stratification or convergent comparison are needed.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1968 §1.3 explicitly qualifies ordinary base change; §§3.1–3.4 formulate stratification. KatzOda1968 provides Gauss–Manin. The perfect-complex countermodel and Kothari2026 Theorem1.1 exhibit distinct algebraic and geometric risks.
why_open: The next pages develop the structure, then withdraw the ordinary characteristic-p stratification hope.
worth: Worth a diagram audit separating derived objects, cohomology modules and stratification; all three occur on the same sheet.

title: Derived Gauss–Manin construction and descent from affine charts
as_he_states: Use Cartan homotopy for formally smooth affines, then construct an absolute canonical connection on a derived direct image in an appendix.
plausible_today: Local lift-independence follows from Cartan’s formula; a global derived construction requires descent. For proper smooth characteristic-zero families the cohomology is locally free with its base-change-compatible integrable Gauss–Manin connection.
state_of_art: KatzOda1968 §§2–3 gives the global construction and explicit connection. The polynomial identity is independently checked, and no finite calculation is represented as a proof of global descent.
why_open: The source explicitly defers the derived construction and distinguishes it from a connection on each cohomology sheaf.
worth: Worth identifying the promised appendix through cross-folder links; the elementary affine identity needs no further research.

title: The withdrawn characteristic-p stratification hope
as_he_states: Hope canonical connections underlie ordinary stratifications; explicitly say this is false for elliptic families in characteristic p, then propose a unified theory.
plausible_today: Ordinary all-order stratification imposes zero p-curvature. Gauss–Manin may have nonzero nilpotent p-curvature; PD/crystalline structures are the appropriate different objects.
state_of_art: Katz1970 §5 defines p-curvature; Katz1984 p183 supplies the Legendre Picard–Fuchs equation. This run computes a nonzero square-zero p-curvature matrix for the smooth proper Legendre family in characteristic3.
why_open: The reason for withdrawal is on the page: elliptic families contradict the hope. The W–M link is then called heuristic.
worth: Worth presenting the explicit obstruction as verification of his own correction, while preserving the PD distinction.

title: Infinitesimal cohomology and singular complex cohomology
as_he_states: Conjecture comparison for all locally finite-type C-schemes, without smoothness, using the infinitesimal site and no differential forms in the definition.
plausible_today: Exactly the locally finite-type infinitesimal-to-singular comparison is true; ambient completion is required when computing it by forms.
state_of_art: Liu2025 Theorems1.1/14.1 prove the locally finite-type complex infinitesimal/singular comparison; Theorem1.2 supplies the completed-ambient computation. Hartshorne1975 IV.1.1 (p89) proves completed algebraic/analytic/singular comparison for finite-type C-schemes embedded in smooth schemes; IV.2.1 (p91) is the formal analytic Poincaré lemma. The earlier unpublished Deligne proof is an attribution reported by Liu, not a source recovered by this run.
why_open: The manuscript calls the smooth case proved and singles out the singular extension as the conjecture.
worth: Worth closing the conjecture with exact scope and publication history; naive singular Ω_X is not the theorem.

title: Čech–Alexander computation and formalization as coefficients
as_he_states: Compute stratification cohomology from diagonal neighbourhoods; make formalization act on differential-operator complexes; construct the cover of the final topos object.
plausible_today: Use the sheaf-level filtered colimit of representables, its inverse-limit coefficient complex, and explicit compatibility/exactness assumptions. The pro-object need not itself be a site object.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1968 §§5.1,6.1–6.3 gives the construction; Fiorot2011 gives a bounded coherent pro version; Liu2025 treats the relevant inverse-limit issues. Scan060 continues on061, where “s’induisent mutuellement” is essential.
why_open: The draft is actively correcting variance, scalar actions and the target category; the package boundary is not a missing manuscript page.
worth: Worth a final categorical diagram and a scan check of the two mutual-induction insertions on061.
